'''Renato Renner''' (born 11 December 1974) is a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] professor for [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]] at the [[ETH Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH)]] in [[Zürich|Zurich]], where he is head of the Research Group for [[Quantum information|Quantum Information Theory]].<ref name="ETHpdf">{{Cite web|title=ETH Zürich - Renato Renner|url=https://www.bi.id.ethz.ch/personensuche/personenDetail/cv/e78b.pdf|access-date=2021-12-09|website=www.bi.id.ethz.ch}}</ref> His research interests include Quantum Information and [[Quantum computing|Computation]], the Foundations of [[Quantum mechanics|Quantum Physics]] and [[Quantum thermodynamics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Renato Renner - Home |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/contrib-81388592781 |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=Author DO Series |doi=<!-- --> |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Renner was born 11 December 1974 in [[Lucerne]], [[Switzerland]], where he received his high school degree in 1994 from Kantonsschule. He then went to study [[physics]] at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL)]] and continued his education at the [[ETH Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH)]] in Zurich, where he graduated in theoretical physics. Renner then joined ETH's department of Computer Science as a Ph.D. student, where he worked in the field of [[Quantum cryptography|Quantum Cryptography]] and specialized in the ''Security of [[Quantum key distribution|Quantum Key Distribution]],'' which became the title of his doctoral thesis in 2005.<ref name="ETHpdf" /><ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Security of quantum key distribution|url=https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/handle/20.500.11850/72791|publisher=ETH Zurich|date=2005|degree=Doctoral Thesis|language=en|first=Renato|last=Renner}}</ref> He continued his scientific career with a two-year [[postdoctoral researcher]] position at the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics of the [[University of Cambridge]], [[United Kingdom]].<ref name="ETHpdf" />

At his return to Switzerland in 2007, Renner started as assistant professor at ETH Zurich and then continued to work from 2012 as associate professor in the Department of Theoretical Physics, where he was promoted to a Full Professor in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ETH Zürich - Renato Renner|url=https://www.bi.id.ethz.ch/personensuche/personenDetail.view?lang=en&pid=E78B|access-date=2021-12-09|website=www.bi.id.ethz.ch|language=en}}</ref> He and his team are especially active in the field of [[Computer security|Cyber Security]].<ref>Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner: [https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/handle/20.500.11850/526535 ''Security in Quantum Cryptography.''] research-collection.ethz.ch, 2021-08-30. Retrieved 2022-07-30.</ref><ref>Christian Speicher: [https://www.nzz.ch/wissenschaft/quantenkryptografie-schluessel-mit-geraete-unabhaengiger-sicherheit-ld.1695123 ''Seit Jahren versprechen Quantenphysiker die absolut sichere Verschlüsselung von Daten. Aber erst jetzt lösen sie dieses Versprechen wirklich ein.''] In: ''Neue Zürcher Zeitung.'' 2022-07-30. Retrieved 2022-07-30.</ref>

== Awards ==
* 2018, ''ALEA Award'' of the AVETH<ref>{{Cite web |title=Renato Renner mit dem ersten ALEA Award ausgezeichnet |url=https://ethz.ch/en/die-eth-zuerich/portraet/aktuelle-ehrungen-und-preise/2017/12/renato-renner-mit-dem-ersten-alea-award-ausgezeichnet.html |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=ethz.ch |language=en}}</ref>
* 2017 and 2011, Teaching Award (''Golden Owl'') from the ''ETH Zurich Physics Student Association''{{citation needed|date=April 2023}}
* 2016, TCC ''Test of Time Award'' from the ''International Association for Cryptologic Research'' ''(IACR)''<ref>{{Cite web |title=TCC Test of Time Award |url=https://www.iacr.org/workshops/tcc/awards.html |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=www.iacr.org |language=en}}</ref>
* 2015, Fellowship at the Stellenbosch Institute for Advanced Study{{citation needed|date=April 2023}}
* 2011, CRM Aisenstadt Chair<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aisenstadt - Renato Renner |url=http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/Renner/ |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=www.crm.umontreal.ca}}</ref>
* 2010 - 2015, ''[[European Research Council|ERC]] Starting Independent Researcher Grant''
* Best Dissertation Award by the German Chapter of the [[Association for Computing Machinery|Association for Computing Machinery (ACM)]]
* 2005, [[ETH Zurich|ETH]] Medal for his PhD thesis
